To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found that the repair models mined from real-world software bugs have a number of interesting properties, which can be exploited to guide automated program fixing, and that these models can be used to predict whether a given patch can fix a bug or not.
We propose a new model-based approach to automated software fixing.

1) we can use the repair models mined from real-world programs to reason on the search space of automated program fixing, 2) the models are useful for predicting the success and cost of automated program fixing and, 3) the models can be used to guide the search for program repair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we model the search space of automated program fixing?
the following question: how can we improve the effectiveness and efficiency of automated program fixing?
the following problem: Given a program and its bug report, automatically fix the bug by applying a sequence of program edits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents an approach to mining repair models for automated program fixing.
we are able to mine repair models for a given bug, which is the first step towards automated program fixing.
the paper presents an empirical study on how to use the repair model to reason on the search space of automated program fixing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new model to capture the repair process of automated program fixing.
we are able to reason on the search space of automated program fixing, and that we are able (and have demonstrated) to find the most promising fix for a program bug.

the repair model can be used as a tool for reasoning on the search space of automated program fixing.
we have developed a novel technique for reasoning on the search space of automated program fixing.
